rationale: This is a mechanical merge of two already-tested archive signals — AccrualCoveredCashLossStress (identical legs and gate) and PersistentNonDepAccrualDeficitStress (the MA(…,3) smoothing) — so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism, and both parents already share ~90% of their cross-sectional variation.

The construction is internally correct (ib − oancf + dpc + apalch algebraically strips the payables channel out of the working-capital accrual gap, matching the hypothesis) and the payables decomposition is a substantive rather than cosmetic refinement of SignedNonDepAccrualCashDrain, though it remains an incremental step within a heavily mined accrual-plus-liquidity family.

Replacing the static retained-deficit/liability-level gate with a solvency-deterioration flow gate (Δlt/sale, Δceq/at) is an economically distinct conditioning variable rather than a relabeling, and the sign logic and expression are consistent.

The accrual-reversal-plus-earnings-deterioration mechanism is coherent and correctly signed, but the Δ(ib/at) leg substantially overlaps the well-known earnings-change/profitability-momentum anomaly and the LAG makes the accrual leg roughly two-year-stale information, so incremental content is uncertain.

The claimed novelty (signed rather than absolute aoloch) was already implemented in DirectionalOpaqueAssetBuildStress and OpaqueAssetBuildShortDebtDrain, so this is a recombination of two archive signals whose gate is also near-redundant (low txt is largely mechanical given low pi, double-counting profitability).

The non-negated complexity term in both legs is deliberate and matches the stated "hold complexity and distress fixed, contrast cash rebuild vs. drain" design, but the resulting signal reduces largely to conditional Δcash-holdings, a partly documented predictor, so the incremental content rests entirely on the conditioning being informative.
